title: Igloos
objective: After this level you can explain how snow houses stay warm.
summary: Iglu means house in Inuktitut. Snow blocks climb an inward-leaning spiral into a dome. Compressed snow insulates, tiered floors hold the warmest air, and a lamp does the rest.

cards.headline: An experienced builder can raise a house of snow in one to two hours.
cards.body: In Inuktitut, iglu simply means "house". The snow iglu, the igloo, was a winter home and hunting-ground shelter of Inuit in Canada and Greenland. So how do you build a warm house out of something frozen?

cards.headline: A spiral of snow
cards.body: Builders pick hard, compact snow and cut large blocks with a knife of whalebone or metal. The top of the first ring is shaved into a slope: the first rung of a spiral. More blocks climb that spiral, each leaning inward, until they close into a dome, with the builder working from inside. Remember Level 5? A dome can rise ring by ring with no frame. An igloo is that trick, in snow.

mascot.line: Level 5's dome, rebuilt from snow in an afternoon. Engineers call that a good day.

cards.headline: Why snow, not ice
cards.body: Hard-packed snow is a good insulator, so the walls hold in body heat and the heat of an oil lamp called a qulliq. Solid ice would do worse: it holds heat less well than compressed snow. Some igloos have tiered floors, so people sleep up high, where it's warmer. Even melting helps: warm inside, bitter cold outside, and any thawing patch freezes again, making the walls stronger.

cards.fact: Inside an igloo, it's often just above freezing.
cards.context: That sounds chilly, and it is. Inuit traditionally kept their fur-lined clothes on indoors during the day. But with several people inside and a lamp burning, an igloo can reach about 15°C. The lamp was the heart of the home, where people cooked, ate, warmed up and talked. Not toasty, but home.

cards.headline: Igloos: warmed up
learned: Snow blocks climb an inward-leaning spiral into a dome
Compressed snow insulates better than ice
Tiered floors and a lamp: often just above freezing, up to about 15°C

questions.prompt: What does the Inuktitut word iglu mean?

options.label: Snow
options.rationale: It's the word for a house, of any material.

options.label: Dome
options.rationale: The dome is the shape; the word means house.

options.label: Winter
options.rationale: Iglu is the word for a house.

questions.explanation: Iglu means 'house' in Inuktitut; the snow iglu is the igloo.

questions.prompt: Why are igloos built from blocks of hard snow rather than solid ice?

options.label: Ice is too heavy to lift
options.rationale: Weight isn't the reason given; heat is.

options.label: Ice melts faster indoors
options.rationale: The point is insulation: snow holds heat better.

options.label: Compressed snow holds in heat better than solid ice
Snow is easier to see through
options.rationale: Clear ice is the one used for windows.

questions.explanation: Hard snow walls are good insulators that keep in body heat and lamp heat; solid ice doesn't retain heat as well as compressed snow.

questions.prompt: Like Level 5's domes, an igloo rises without a wooden frame. How do its blocks manage it?

options.label: They hang from a central pole until the snow freezes
options.rationale: No pole: the blocks support themselves.

options.label: They climb a spiral, leaning inward until they close into a dome
They're stacked straight up, then bent inward
options.rationale: Snow blocks can't bend; each is set leaning in.

options.label: They rest on a hidden frame of whalebone
options.rationale: Whalebone is for the knife, not a frame.

questions.explanation: The first ring is shaved into a sloping rung; blocks follow the spiral inward to a dome, just as Level 5's domes rise ring by ring without centering.
